components.text: Read together, these numbers left the editors with one plain impression: the readers are still here. In ten years the share of readers and the books they read barely moved, and print reading grew by about five minutes a day. What shrank was the time once kept for papers and magazines.

A magazine can make the pieces worth finishing easier to finish: on paper, in your headphones, at a library's long tables. The next page lists our plans for the year, each with its reason. How far we get, we will tell you in next year's letter.
We will not cut our pieces short to fight screens for a few seconds.

notes: Here is where we land. Readers have not left books. What they left is the fixed time once given to newspapers and magazines, the morning paper and the few pages before bed, which now goes to the phone. That is not bad news, and not entirely good news either. We will not shorten our pieces to chase screens, which already have plenty. We want to do something else: make the pieces worth finishing easier to finish. The next page says how.
